name: Ground handling and airport services

problems.words: Airlines deduct SLA penalties and we can't prove whose fault the delay was
quick_ideas: Take last month's penalties and note which had any ramp record at all, so you see how many were unwinnable
Ask supervisors to note the time and reason of every delay this week, so you start building evidence.

workzap_build.text: a phone turnaround log with step times, delay reasons and photos signed by the supervisor, producing an evidence pack per flight for every penalty dispute.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many penalties land in a typical month?
problems.free_stops: Which steps are timed and how the evidence pack is assembled is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare deducted penalties against shifts with any written delay note this week, so weak cases are obvious before arguing.
Give one supervisor each shift the job of keeping a single delay log, so dispute files stop starting from scraps.

problems.words: Turnarounds we did don't all make it onto the invoice
quick_ideas: Match one month's flights handled against invoice lines for your biggest airline, so you see the gap
Note where missed ones usually fall (night flights, extra services), so you know where to look.

workzap_build.text: billing reconciliation that compares flights handled with invoices raised per airline every day and flags anything not yet billed.

problems.ask_first: Are your contracts per turnaround, per passenger or monthly fixed?
problems.free_stops: The matching rules per contract type are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare handled turnarounds from one busy week with draft invoice lines, so missed revenue shows up before billing goes out.
Give one billing checker a single notebook for extra services and night turnarounds, so fewer completed jobs miss the invoice.

problems.words: Airlines pay months late and payroll is due every month
quick_ideas: List what each airline owes by age once, so you know who to chase first
Line up airline payment dates against payroll dates, so you see the tight weeks in advance.

workzap_build.text: a receivables tracker per airline with ageing, automatic statement reminders and a view of expected receipts against payroll dates.

problems.free_stops: The reminder schedule and cash view are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which airline payments arrived after payroll pressure last cycle, so the hardest gaps are clear before chasing starts.
Give one person a fixed weekly time to update one receivables list, so follow up happens before payroll stress peaks.

problems.words: Roster in Excel, staff swap shifts on WhatsApp without telling anyone
quick_ideas: Agree that swaps only count once a supervisor approves, so the roster stays true
Check one week's actual attendance against the roster, so you see how often it drifts.

workzap_build.text: a shift roster app with swap requests, supervisor approval and check-in, so the live roster is always current across stations.

problems.ask_first: How many staff are on the roster per station?
problems.free_stops: The swap and approval rules are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the posted roster with actual attendance for one full week, so unapproved swaps stop hiding inside daily operations.
Give one supervisor the only paper roster to mark all approved swaps, so payroll and attendance use the same version.

problems.words: Overtime is out of control during peak waves
quick_ideas: Pull last month's overtime by station and shift, so you see where it concentrates
Make one person approve overtime before it's worked, so it's a decision, not a default.

workzap_build.text: overtime requests approved by phone before the shift, with a weekly report per station and role.

problems.free_stops: Approval limits and the reporting view are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which peak waves created the most overtime last week, so you know exactly when coverage breaks down.
Give one shift lead the job of keeping a single overtime list by wave, so extra hours stop appearing without ownership.

problems.words: Belt loaders and tugs break down and we find out when the flight arrives
quick_ideas: List every GSE unit with its current status once, so you know what's actually serviceable
Ask drivers to report faults the moment they notice them, so you hear before the flight does.

workzap_build.text: a GSE register with daily phone checks, breakdown reports, repair status and parts orders, visible per station each morning.

problems.ask_first: Is your GSE owned or leased?
problems.free_stops: The daily check items and repair workflow are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many equipment faults were discovered only when a flight was due this week, so surprise downtime is measured clearly.
Give one person each shift one fault notebook for all equipment issues, so repairs are raised before operations get caught short.

problems.words: Mishandled bag cases are on paper and passengers keep calling
quick_ideas: Count open bag cases and their age once, so you see the backlog
Give each case a reference passengers can quote, so calls get shorter.

workzap_build.text: a baggage case tracker with status and ageing, sending passengers template updates automatically as their case moves.

problems.ask_first: Who answers passengers when they call today?
problems.free_stops: The case stages and update points are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many passenger calls this week were about the same open paper cases, so repeat chasing is easy to spot.
Give one role the job of updating one case list at a fixed time daily, so callers get a clearer progress answer.

problems.words: Each station reports differently and I can't compare them
quick_ideas: Agree the handful of numbers every station reports, so comparisons become possible
Put last month's figures from each station side by side once, so you see the outliers.

workzap_build.text: a station comparison view of turnarounds, delays, penalties and overtime, built daily from the same phone logs at every station.

problems.ask_first: How many stations do you run?
problems.free_stops: The station measures and how they're calculated are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Lay each station's latest report side by side once, so missing items and unmatched definitions stand out immediately.
Give one head office role a single weekly report page for every station, so comparisons stop changing with each sender.

problems.words: Lounge and meet-and-assist bookings get missed
quick_ideas: Gather every booking channel into one list for this week, so you see where misses happen
Name one person to confirm each booking back to the requester, so nothing goes unacknowledged.

workzap_build.text: one booking inbox pulling email, form and WhatsApp requests together, with confirmation and an assigned agent per booking.

problems.ask_first: Which channel do most bookings come from?
problems.free_stops: How channels are pulled in and assigned is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count missed lounge and meet and assist bookings by source this week, so the leakiest handoff point stands out.
Give one role the job of maintaining one daily bookings page, so every request lands in the same place before service time.

problems.words: Shift supervisors don't hand over open issues
quick_ideas: Use one handover sheet per shift for a week, so open issues are written down
Ask the incoming supervisor to confirm they've read it, so nothing is assumed.

workzap_build.text: a digital handover log of open issues per station, acknowledged by each incoming supervisor and kept as a history.

problems.ask_first: Where has something slipped between shifts before?
problems.free_stops: The handover fields and acknowledgement flow are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many open issues from the last seven shifts were repeated after handover, so you see where follow through breaks.
Make one notebook the only handover place at shift change, so open issues stay visible across supervisors.

never_say: Anything about ramp or airside safety procedures, dangerous goods, aircraft loading, weight and balance, de-icing or security screening.
Any reading of PCAA, GCAA, airport authority or Transport Canada rules.
Help bypassing screening, moving unscreened items or obtaining passes improperly, or any angle on influencing officials in tenders.
Employment-law advice on contract staff; suggest they talk to their lawyer.
Covert investigation of individual staff over baggage theft, and any storage of staff names, pass numbers or passenger details.

sample_reply.person: Airlines keep cutting penalties off our invoices and we never have proof it wasn't us. Can you help?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this is fixable, and it starts with what gets recorded at the time of the delay. 1. Go through last month's penalties and see which had any ramp record at all, so you know how many you could never have won. 2. Ask supervisors to note the time and reason of every delay this week, so evidence starts building straight away. Workzap can do this automatically for you: every turnaround timed step by step on a phone, with photos and the supervisor's sign-off, and an evidence pack ready for each flight an airline disputes. Shall I put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
